attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own Substack post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The claim is a firm present-tense statement about the current METR suite at 80% and 95% success. The drafter kept both thresholds and added nothing to them.

contract.note: Reading headroom as the suite still holding much longer tasks than Mythos's horizon at a given reliability is a fair, ordinary reading of his point that Mythos saturates the suite only at 50%. The 95% part rests on the fitted curve, and the contract says so openly.

evidence.note: METR's own data for the early Mythos checkpoint give an 80% horizon of about 3.1 hours, far below the roughly 16-hour measurable ceiling. The fitted logistic curve implies a shorter 95% horizon. This was available before the evaluation date.
Names the March early checkpoint and gives a 50% horizon of at least 16 hours, near the suite's measurement limit. This sets the ceiling against which the 80% horizon is compared.

reviews.rationale: METR's data put Mythos's 80% horizon at about 3.1 hours, against a suite that can measure up to about 16 hours, so there is substantial headroom at 80%. Under METR's documented fitted curve, the 95% horizon is shorter still (about 27 minutes), which meets the contract's support condition. This 95% figure is derived from the curve, not separately validated. Nothing in the packet shows the suite saturated at 80%.
